summary: Tenant-triggered connection slab fragmentation after synchronized retry burst causing upstream resets and elevated 5xx
description: Issue summary: BrightForms reported sustained 5xx rate (502/503) beginning 2026-03-10 02:12 UTC affecting their Dedicated tenant in us-east. Errors correlate with a tight burst pattern from the tenant's clients: many short streaming sessions with aggressive client-side retrying. The API gateway observed connection slab fragmentation and high ephemeral FD churn, followed by upstream runtime thread saturation and subsequent connection resets. Impact: customer-facing failures for BrightForms' production endpoints (webhooks and interactive chat), increased 99th latency, and automated failover to fallback model instances which exacerbated load.
impact: ~18% error rate across BrightForms' requests at peak (02:12-02:45 UTC). Several requests returned 502/503, streaming sessions dropped. Customer reported user-visible errors and retries leading to revenue-impacting outages for a subset of their customers.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Simulate 1,200 short-lived streaming sessions per second from a single tenant IP pool with randomized 1-3s active intervals.
2) Configure client to retry failed requests aggressively (backoff 50-200ms) for up to 3 retries.
3) Observe API gateway ephemeral FD usage rise and connection slab fragmentation over 60s.
4) Monitor upstream runtime thread pool queue length and runtime log for OOM/watchdog resets.
5) Repeat with keepalive disabled on client sockets to increase churn and confirm amplification.
observed_behavior: API gateway connection slab fragmentation (conn_slab_free < threshold), ephemeral FD count growth, proxy threads queuing, serving-runtime thread exhaustion followed by worker SIGTERM and reconnect churn. Error stream showed mostly 502 on first failure then 503 after failover attempts.
expected_behavior: Transient client bursts should be absorbed by connection pooling and autoscaler without causing upstream threadpool starvation or sustained 5xx for the tenant.

investigation_notes: 2026-03-10 03:00 - Initial triage: spike correlates to customer traffic pattern; other tenants unaffected at host level until runtime threadpool saturation observed.

Connection slab fragmentation appears when ephemeral connections are allocated and freed at high rate; allocator fails to coalesce leading to FD scarcity for accept(): triggers proxy-level immediate 502.
Serving-runtime shows unusually high thread queue length and nearly all threads blocked on socket reads; heap usage not growing dramatically — indicates I/O wait rather than memory leak.
NVML reset logged on one runtime host after repeated reconnects; on that host GPU reset caused brief task restarts which amplified request retries and further churn.
Grafana: apigw_ephemeral_fd_count increased from baseline 120 -> 3,800 over 90s; runtime_thread_queue_p95 spiked from 20 -> 980.
Hypothesis: customer-side retry/backlog pattern + short-lived streaming sessions cause fragmentation and proxy fd exhaustion which cascades into runtime thread starvation and occasional NVML resets.
Tested workaround: throttling tenant to 400 concurrent streams prevented slab fragmentation in canary and eliminated 5xx within 10 minutes.

Related internal ticket INT-4412 tracks a similar but lower-severity slab fragmentation incident last quarter; differences: that event was triggered by bot traffic on public endpoints, this is tenant-isolated dedicated traffic.
Attached artifacts: grafana panels, pcap capture (s3://redwood-support/artifacts/SUP-827364/pcap.gz), runtime logs (s3://redwood-support/artifacts/SUP-827364/runtime-logs.tar.gz).

resolution: Workaround: Applied tenant-level concurrent stream throttle to 400 streams which removed fd exhaustion and returned error rate to baseline within ~10 minutes. Permanent fix: proxy allocator coalescing improvements and keepalive/conn-reuse tuning deployed to staging; scheduled canary rollout to us-east 2026-03-14 02:00 UTC. Customer instructed to increase client retry backoff and enable TCP keepalive as interim guard.
root_cause: Sustained, synchronized short-lived streaming sessions combined with aggressive client-side retries caused fragmentation in the API gateway's ephemeral connection slab. FD scarcity led to accept() failures and 502 responses; proxy-level retries and repeated reconnects caused serving-runtime threadpool to block on socket reads and in one host triggered an NVML driver reset, amplifying 5xx.
